summary: Space biology is the study of how living organisms survive, grow, and develop in space under different environmental conditions. Scientists study plants, animals, and microorganisms to understand the effects of microgravity, radiation, and extreme temperatures on living things. Growing plants on the Moon and Mars is especially important because plants can provide food and oxygen. Researchers are investigating how to grow plants in special capsules using artificial light, controlled temperature, humidity, and recycled water. Experiments such as Iran's Kavoshgar-3 mission, which sent mice, turtles, and worms into space in 2010, help scientists understand how space affects living organisms. In the future, space biology may help humans build sustainable habitats on the Moon and Mars, produce their own food, and live in space for long periods.

Detailed Information About Our Project: Space Biology

What is the purpose of our project and how does it work?

Our project aims to investigate how living organisms survive, grow, and develop in space. We study how plants, animals, and microorganisms are affected by space conditions. We especially focus on methods of growing plants on the Moon and Mars. We research how plants can be grown in special capsules using artificial light, controlled temperature, humidity, and recycled water.

What are the benefits of our project?

The most important benefit of our project is that it can help astronauts grow their own food in space in the future. Plants can provide oxygen and meet nutritional needs. They can also help save water and other resources in space. In addition, our project helps us understand how living organisms adapt to space conditions.

What is the intended impact of the project?

The main goal of our project is to help humans live on the Moon and Mars for long periods in the future. We aim to create sustainable living spaces, grow plants, and use natural resources efficiently. In this way, we hope to contribute to scientific research that could allow humans to live in space without depending entirely on Earth.

What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software did we use to develop our project?

Our project focuses on research and providing information. No specific programming language, electronic hardware, or experimental equipment is mentioned in our poster. We used scientific research, information about space biology, and visual design studies to develop our project. In the future, the project could be improved by using sensors and automatic systems to control temperature, humidity, light, and water levels.

How creative is our project?

Our project is a very creative and future-oriented idea because it focuses on growing food outside Earth, especially on the Moon and Mars. Growing plants in space, studying how animals respond to space conditions, and creating artificial habitats bring together different scientific fields.

What factors did our team consider?

Our team considered the following factors during our research:

  • The effects of gravity on living organisms.
  • Radiation and extreme temperature changes in space.
  • The water, light, and oxygen plants need.
  • Temperature and humidity control.
  • Recycling water and other resources.
  • The characteristics of Moon and Mars soil.
  • The conditions necessary for humans to live in space for long periods.

Conclusion:

Our project introduces an important research area for the future of life in space. Understanding how plants and other living organisms can survive in space conditions may help create sustainable habitats on the Moon and Mars in the future. Our biggest goal is to contribute to a future in which humans can live safely and healthily beyond Earth.
